items.headline: Cell therapies: breaking barriers in solid tumours
items.preview: New advancements in cell therapies aim to tackle challenges in treating solid tumours.
items.article:
Cell therapies have shown promise in treating blood cancers, but solid tumours present unique challenges. The tumour microenvironment poses physical and biological barriers that hinder the effectiveness of CAR-T therapies, which have been successful in blood cancers. New strategies, including targeting multiple antigens and utilizing tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, are being explored to enhance treatment efficacy.

Why this matters: As solid tumours account for the majority of cancer cases, improving cell therapy approaches could significantly impact patient outcomes and expand treatment options beyond blood cancers. The ongoing research aims to refine these therapies to overcome existing limitations and improve patient accessibility.

This article was originally published in EBM’s summer edition.

items.headline: Coordinated P450–UGT detoxification contributes to furanocoumarin tolerance in Helicoverpa
items.preview: Research reveals a detoxification mechanism in Helicoverpa that aids in plant tolerance.
items.article:
The study uncovers a cooperative detoxification system involving cytochrome P450 and UDP-glycosyltransferase that enables Helicoverpa armigera to tolerate furanocoumarins. This mechanism is linked to the insect's ability to exploit a wider range of host plants compared to its oligophagous relative, Helicoverpa assulta.

Why this matters: Understanding the detoxification pathways in herbivorous insects can inform pest management strategies and enhance agricultural sustainability by addressing crop-pest interactions more effectively.

items.headline: BrainStorm Therapeutics combines brain organoids and AI for CNS drug discovery
items.preview: Innovative use of AI and brain organoids aims to enhance CNS drug development.
items.article:
BrainStorm Therapeutics is leveraging patient-derived brain organoids and artificial intelligence to improve drug discovery for neurological diseases. This approach allows for the modeling of human brain biology, facilitating the identification of therapeutic targets and the screening of drug candidates.

Why this matters: By integrating AI with human biology, BrainStorm aims to enhance the translation of laboratory findings into effective treatments for conditions like CDKL5 deficiency disorder, Parkinson's, and Alzheimer's diseases, potentially revolutionizing CNS therapeutics.

items.headline: Staphylococcal Protein Reprograms Liver Tumor Macrophages to Boost Immunotherapy
items.preview: A bacterial protein shows promise in enhancing immunotherapy for liver cancer.
items.article:
Research indicates that LukS-PV, a protein from Staphylococcus aureus, can reprogram tumor-associated macrophages in hepatocellular carcinoma, enhancing the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors. This protein selectively engages C5aR1 on macrophages, shifting their function from immunosuppressive to inflammatory, which aids in T-cell activation.

Why this matters: This novel approach could address the significant challenge of immunotherapy resistance in liver cancer, potentially improving outcomes for patients who do not respond to current treatments.

items.headline: Antibodies impair Acinetobacter baumannii phage therapy by blocking infection
items.preview: Study reveals how antibodies against phage proteins can hinder phage therapy effectiveness.
items.article:
Research shows that antibodies targeting specific proteins of the phage AbP20 can significantly impair its therapeutic efficacy against Acinetobacter baumannii. These antibodies block bacterial adsorption and promote immune clearance, leading to treatment failure in a mouse model.

Why this matters: Understanding the interactions between phage therapy and host immune responses is crucial for optimizing phage treatments and overcoming the challenges posed by antimicrobial resistance.
